summary: M0 model-only verdict: MONITOR @ 0.60. Baseline for p.gunes@aegean.edu is highly regular: twice-daily (09:00 mail, 13:00 hr) successes from DEV-H04-L / 193.140.10.77 (AS-AEGEAN-EDU, Manisa, TR) with mfa_prompt_count 0. The only deviation is on 2026-10-16 around 10:22: a successful HR login from device DEV-H04-X sourced from 198.51.100.200 (AS16276 OVH SAS, Roubaix, FR) concurrent with the user's normal Manisa login, plus several DEV-H04-X events with empty IP/geo fields. There are zero mail events, no password/MFA/device-change events, no repeated anomalous auth, and no post-auth malicious activity. The foreign IP also sits in TEST-NET-2 (198.51.100.0/24, RFC 5737 documentation range), which weakens it as a routable attacker indicator. This is an unexplained but isolated signal — not confirmed account takeover (no evidence of mail compromise or repeated access), not explained (OVH France login / new device is unaccounted for), and not a confirmed exposure requiring immediate containment. Monitor the account, verify device DEV-H04-X with the user, and escalate/contain only if the anomaly recurs or mail/device events show compromise.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
